title: Spotify says it won’t recommend music from ‘AI Personas’
slides: Spotify bans AI personas, but who defines authenticity?
New policy targets cloned voices without artist consent.
Yet labels quietly license AI vocals for hit songs.
Your playlists will hide these tracks, not remove them.
Check your Discover Weekly for surprising new exclusions.
thread_text:
1. Who owns your voice?

Spotify's new ban on AI personas leaves a loophole: labels can still quietly license AI vocals for hits, as long as they have permission.

2. The hidden track

Those AI-generated songs won't be removed from your playlists—just hidden from view. You might be listening to one right now without knowing.

3. Authenticity is for sale

While Spotify polices cloned voices without artist consent, record labels are cashing in by licensing AI vocals for chart-topping tracks. The real gatekeepers? Money.

4. The exclusions start now

Your Discover Weekly just got a silent overhaul. AI tracks that fail the new authenticity test are being weeded out, but the ones that pass the licensing bar stay.

5. Check your playlist today

Look at your Discover Weekly this week. If you spot a song you don't remember saving, ask: is this a creator, or a clone? How would you know?

instagram.caption:
Your Discover Weekly just got a silent overhaul 🎧 Spotify won’t recommend music from “AI personas” anymore—but those tracks aren’t deleted, just hidden from view.

The ban targets cloned voices used without an artist’s consent. The catch? Labels can still license AI vocals for hit songs, as long as they have permission. So the policy blocks fakes, not paid-for ones 💸

For you as a creator or listener: your playlists may already contain AI-generated tracks you’ve never noticed. They’ll stay, just unlisted from recommendations.

Open Spotify now. Scroll your Discover Weekly. Can you tell which songs are human-made—or does it even matter to you? 🤔
